predecessors.name: Tang dynasty
predecessors.text: Xiazhou, Youzhou, Suizhou, Yinzhou and later Jingbian, granted to Tuoba Sigong in 881

successors.name: Western Xia (Great Xia)
successors.text: the Tangut state of Li Jiqian, named King of the Xia State by the Liao in 990 (Cliopatria's Western Xia row starts in 990)

successors.name: Song dynasty (Northern and Southern Song)
successors.text: the Dingnan Jiedushi, which Li Jipeng surrendered to the Song court in 982

ledger.x: 881: the Tangut Tuoba clan gets the Dingnan Circuit.
990: the Tangut state becomes the Xia.

wars.name: Li Jiqian's rising against the Song
wars.outcome: Li Jiqian escaped the Song attack of 984, took Yinzhou in 985, paid tribute to the Liao from 986 and was named King of the Xia State in 990; the Song recognised him later (Li Jiqian page: Dingnan jiedushi 998-1004).

certainty.note: The pages name four or five prefectures and a centre at Yulin but no frontier; the circle is a reading.
